questions.subject: Physics
questions.category: Laws of Motion :: Multi-Concept Physical Modeling (Type 2)
questions.question: In a wedge-block system in [Laws of Motion], a smooth wedge of mass $M = 3\text{ kg}$ with incline angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ is free to slide horizontally on a frictionless floor. A block of mass $m_0 = 1\text{ kg}$ slides down a distance $s = 2\text{ m}$ along the face of the wedge relative to the incline. What is the horizontal displacement of the wedge?
questions.solution: Since horizontal net external force is zero, center of mass position is invariant horizontally: $M \Delta x_W + m_0(\Delta x_W - s \cos 30^\circ) = 0 \implies \Delta x_W = \frac{m_0 s \cos 30^\circ}{M + m_0} = \frac{1 \times 2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{3 + 1} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\text{ m}$.
questions.explanation: Analyze the physical model and equations in Laws of Motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.category: Laws of Motion :: Numerical Derivation
questions.question: A block of mass $m = 10\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal floor with static friction coefficient $\mu_s = 0.5$. A horizontal force of $F = 20\text{ N}$ is applied to the block. If $F < f_s^{\max}$, what is the magnitude of the frictional force exerted by the floor on the block in Newtons?
questions.solution: Maximum static friction is $f_s^{\max} = \mu_s m g = 0.5 \times 10 \times 9.8 = 49\text{ N}$ (or $50\text{ N}$ with $g=10$). Since applied force $F = 20\text{ N} \le 40\text{ N} < f_s^{\max}$, the block remains at rest and static friction exactly balances the applied force: $f_s = F = 20\text{ N}$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative physical laws in Laws of Motion.
